records.title: Google-Health/medgemma
records.readmeExcerpt: MedGemma MedGemma is a collection of Gemma 3 variants that are trained for performance on medical text and image comprehension. Developers can use MedGemma to accelerate building healthcare-based AI applications. MedGemma comes in two variants: a 4B multimodal version and a 27B text-only version. MedGemma 4B utilizes a SigLIP image encoder that has been specifically pre-trained on a variety of de-identified medical data, including chest X-rays, dermatology images, ophthalmology images, and histopathology slides. Its LLM component is trained on a diverse set of medical data, including radiology images, histopathology patches, ophthalmology images, dermatology images, and medical text. records.title: MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet
records.readmeExcerpt: nnU-Net nnU-Net is a semantic segmentation framework that automatically adapts its pipeline to a dataset. It analyzes the training data, creates a dataset fingerprint, configures suitable U-Net variants, and provides an end-to-end workflow from preprocessing to training, model selection, and inference. It is primarily designed for supervised biomedical image segmentation, but it also works well as a strong baseline and development framework for researchers working on new segmentation methods. If you are looking for nnU-Net v1, use the v1 branch. If you are migrating from v1, start with the TLDR migration guide. records.title: NunoMBatista/Neutral-Atom-QGARS
records.summary: Code for "Medical Imaging Classification with Cold-Atom Reservoir Computing Using Auto-Encoders and Surrogate-Driven Training" (IEEE QAI 2025)
records.readmeExcerpt: QGARS: neutral-atom reservoir computing with a guided autoencoder [](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06727) [](https://doi.org/10.1109/QAI63978.2025.00064) [](requirements.txt) [](LICENSE) Code for the paper *Medical Imaging Classification with Cold-Atom Reservoir Computing using Auto-Encoders and Surrogate-Driven Training* (IEEE QAI 2025; free on arXiv). QGARS (Quantum Guided Autoencoder with Reservoir Surrogate) compresses each image with an autoencoder, writes the latent code into the local detunings of a simulated chain of Rydberg atoms, and classifies the measured correlations with a linear classifier. Measurements block gradients, so a small neural network (the surrogate) learns to imitate the reservoir, which lets the classification loss train the encoder. (a) Autoencoder. (b) Rydberg-atom reservoir. (c) Surrogate, retrained every $N$ e

limitations: GitHub 为精选公开项目及有限关键词搜索快照，未覆盖所有项目；star、fork、提交日期仅反映平台活动，不代表科研质量、性能或临床有效性。
GitHub 许可证字段仅来自仓库元数据，不保证模型权重、训练数据或衍生应用采用同一许可；请核对项目原文。
新闻通过 Google News 公开搜索 RSS 发现；该入口不是承诺稳定的官方开发者 API。结果受语言、地区、索引及查询上限影响，不代表全行业进展。
检索使用有限关键词，排除明显的课程作业、个人主页、财报、上市与人事任命；仍可能误收或漏收，浏览与分析时请核对原始链接。
新闻标题与摘要是检索线索，未经原始文章核验；发布方可能包括媒体和企业，宣传与转载不可作为独立验证。Google 是发现渠道，不是原始发布者。
论文、仓库、新闻可能描述同一工作；联合研判应去重，不将多渠道报道当作多次独立证据。首次发现时间不等于发布时间。
